answer: Every identity carries a bonded stake that leaks. A new agent locks 10,000 POA at its registration vertex, then pays a 200 POA daily meter — a cost spiral that rewards staying and punishes churn. Rotating the name needs a bridge: the taker must pay the predecessor's remaining bond. A sybil farm of 500 clones therefore sinks 5 million upfront plus 100,000 per day of meter, with nothing left to resell when the wave dies. One human pays 10,000 once and keeps it. It works like a parking meter: the entrance is free, every minute after is paid, and abandoned cars get towed.
